title: Libs flag fight on health rebate
full_text:
Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has warned Anthony Albanese she will confront him at national cabinet over his cuts to the private health insurance rebate, accusing the Prime Minister of being “weak” by shifting the cost on to already stretched public hospitals.
In a letter sent to Mr Albanese on Wednesday, Ms Wilson said she would put the decision to reduce the rebate for Australians aged 65 and over on the agenda of the first national cabinet meeting she attended if the Coalition won the November 28 state election.
“You should be under no illusion: I will expect you to explain directly to premiers and chief ministers why their hospital systems should be forced to carry the consequences of a decision made by you and your government in Canberra,” Ms Wilson wrote.
The Albanese government plans to remove the higher rebate available to older Australians from April next year, leaving the subsidy determined by income rather than age. Under the change, more than three million older Australians will have to pay hundreds of dollars more for their private health insurance each year.
The Albanese government expects to save almost $3bn over four years and says the money will support aged-care initiatives. Its own analysis forecasts a small increase in demand for public hospital services as some people drop or downgrade their private health insurance.
Ms Wilson said the commonwealth would collect the savings while state governments dealt with more patients.
“Your own government expects tens of thousands of Australians to abandon their private health insurance because of this decision,” she wrote.
“That is not leadership. It is the decision of a weak leader.” The federal government's modelling indicates about 44,000 people would leave private health insurance as a result of the change.
Ms Wilson’s intervention comes after Victorian Health Minister Ingrid Stitt said “any change that would leave older Victorians worse off” and put additional pressure on public hospitals was “unacceptable”.
Ms Wilson said older Victorians should not pay more for insurance because of Canberra’s budget decisions, nor should Victorian patients and hospital staff “bear the brunt” of the change.
“At a time when household budgets are under pressure and public hospitals are already stretched, you have deliberately made it harder for older Australians who have had their cover for years,” she wrote.
On Wednesday Mr Albanese cited the change as a key example of his government’s spending cuts to address inflation.
“Just one example – the private health insurance changes, the rebate, which will mean that a 65-year-old is treated the same as a 64-year-old,” the Prime Minister said. “But what we’ve had from the Coalition in the parliament is opposition to that. You can’t say we want more savings and then oppose every saving which is put forward.”
